cards.front: Strongest single risk factor for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is breech presentation; other risks include female sex, family history, and [___].
cards.context:
Breech position, female sex, family history and oligohydramnios increase DDH risk ([meta-analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39853978/)).

Prematurity alone is not an established risk factor ([review](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12887-023-04083-1)).

cards.front: A woman with placenta accreta has had her placenta left in situ after birth under specialist care. Which antimetabolite should not be given to hasten placental resolution? [___]
cards.context:
Methotrexate is not recommended for placenta accreta spectrum. Late pregnancy placenta has few rapidly dividing cells, so the drug has very limited effect.

It can suppress the bone marrow and raise the risk of sepsis.

cards.front: Chorionicity in twins must be determined by 14 weeks; lambda sign indicates DCDA, T sign indicates [___].
cards.context:
Lambda (λ) sign = a triangular wedge of placental tissue pushing into the base of the dividing membrane → dichorionic (DCDA).

T sign = the membrane meets the placenta at a right angle with no wedge of tissue → monochorionic (MCDA). Both are reliable ONLY in the first trimester (thick membrane, visible placental insertion).

Mis-classification matters: MCDA share one placenta — 2-weekly scans from 16 weeks (TTTS 10-15%, TAPS, selective FGR); DCDA need 4-weekly from 20 weeks.

cards.front: In postpartum haemorrhage, crystalloid above about [___] is avoided where possible, because it worsens dilutional coagulopathy.
cards.context:
Crystalloid restores circulating volume but not fibrinogen, platelets or red cells.

Once loss is large, extra clear fluid dilutes the clotting factors that remain, so the next bleed is harder to stop.

Blood and blood products are therefore preferred once she is unstable or still bleeding.

cards.front: [___] is endometrial cancer until proven otherwise. Endometrial thickness >4mm on TVUS warrants biopsy.
cards.context:
Any bleeding after 12 months of amenorrhoea is abnormal — ~10% of women with postmenopausal bleeding turn out to have endometrial cancer, so it always triggers investigation.

The 4mm cut-off works because cancer rarely arises in a thin, atrophic endometrium; a stripe ≤4mm has a negative predictive value over 99%. Above that, you cannot exclude malignancy on imaging alone and need tissue.

cards.front: In kernicterus, unconjugated bilirubin deposits preferentially in the [___] and auditory brainstem nuclei, later producing the tetrad of choreoathetoid cerebral palsy, high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, upward-gaze palsy, and dental enamel dysplasia.
cards.context:
Only the lipid-soluble unconjugated fraction crosses the blood-brain barrier, and it is selectively toxic to the globus pallidus, subthalamic nucleus, and auditory nuclei.

The whole point of screening <24 h jaundice is to phototherapy or exchange-transfuse before this deposition becomes irreversible.

cards.front: Prolonged neonatal jaundice with a raised conjugated bilirubin, pale stools and dark urine is [___] until proven otherwise, and needs surgery within ~60 days.
cards.context:
The timing framework: <24 h = always pathological (haemolysis/sepsis); day 2-3 to ~7 = usually physiological; >14 d (term) = prolonged, always needs a split (conjugated vs unconjugated) bilirubin.

A raised CONJUGATED (direct) fraction with pale stools and dark urine is biliary atresia until excluded, because the Kasai portoenterostomy must be done within ~60 days to preserve the liver.

cards.front: When assessing a pregnancy of uncertain location, serial βhCG measurements are compared about [___] hours apart.
cards.context:
When pregnancy location or viability is uncertain, compare serum βhCG measurements about 48 hours apart; the trend does not diagnose location by itself.

A rise greater than 63% suggests a developing IUP, while a smaller rise, plateau or fall needs clinical review and repeat imaging. A viable pregnancy does not have to double in 48 hours.

cards.front: A woman in labour needs antibiotic prophylaxis for group B streptococcus. Which macrolide should be avoided because resistance is common? [___]
cards.context:
Benzylpenicillin intravenous is the antibiotic of choice for intrapartum GBS prophylaxis.

Erythromycin is not recommended, because resistance rates are high.

cards.front: Mastitis treatment: continue breastfeeding from affected side + [___] for Staph aureus coverage; abscess if fluctuant mass develops.
cards.context:
Mastitis is bacterial breast infection, almost always Staph aureus seeded through cracked nipples or milk duct stasis.

Antibiotics: flucloxacillin 500 mg four times daily (QID) for 5-7 days (cephalexin/clindamycin if pen allergic); analgesia + warm compresses.

Distinguish from engorgement (bilateral, no fever) and cracked nipples alone (visible cracks, painful latch).

cards.front: ECV for breech is offered from 36 weeks (nulliparous) or [___] weeks (multiparous); overall success ~50%.
cards.context:
ECV is manual rotation of breech baby to cephalic by abdominal manipulation. Done at 36-37 weeks (earlier baby may turn back, later uterus too tight + fluid too low); 36w threshold for nulliparous, 37w for multiparous.

Success ~50% overall, ~70% with multiparity/posterior placenta/adequate liquor (DVP >3 cm)/non-engaged breech/operator experience.

After successful ECV, baby usually stays cephalic; failed ECV → planned CS at 39 weeks.

cards.front: Physiological anaemia of pregnancy stays normocytic on the film, so a falling mean cell volume instead points to superimposed [___] deficiency.
cards.context:
The trap is calling every low third-trimester haemoglobin 'iron deficiency'.

Pure haemodilution does not change red-cell size, so normal indices with ferritin >30 µg/L are expected; a dropping MCV or ferritin <30 µg/L means true deficiency has been superimposed and needs treatment.

cards.front: Complete arrest of progress despite adequate contractions defines [___] labour.
cards.context:
Arrest is the usual word for obstructed labour: the cervix or the head has stopped despite adequate contractions. Slow forward change is a different pattern.

The distinction stops a labour that is still moving being treated as if it had stopped. Both patterns still need the whole clinical picture.

cards.front: Jaundice that appears within the first [___] of life is treated as pathological until proven otherwise.
cards.context: Timing is the triage tool. Jaundice in the first 24 hours is always pathological (think haemolysis — e.g. ABO/Rh, G6PD) and needs urgent bilirubin measurement.

cards.front: Lactation hormones: prolactin (anterior pituitary) drives milk production; [___] (posterior pituitary) triggers let-down. The latter is inhibited by stress and pain.
cards.context:
Lactation runs on two complementary hormones. Prolactin (anterior pituitary) drives MILK PRODUCTION, rising with each suckling stimulus and peaking at night.

Oxytocin (posterior pituitary) drives the LET-DOWN reflex, contracting myoepithelial cells to eject stored milk.

Oxytocin release is conditioned to multiple cues but exquisitely sensitive to stress, pain, alcohol, embarrassment — these inhibit let-down even when supply is fine.

cards.front: When endometriosis is suspected and pregnancy is not being attempted, first-line hormonal treatment is a combined oral contraceptive or a [___].
cards.context:
Oral, injection, implant, and intrauterine progestogens are grouped with the combined oral contraceptive as first-line options. Choice is shared and matched to preference, because pain improvement is similar.

Review pain relief and tolerability after three months. People actively trying to become pregnant are not prescribed these hormones for endometriosis.

cards.front: Early syphilis is treated with one intramuscular dose of benzathine penicillin; late latent syphilis needs [___].
cards.context:
Diagnosis is serology: a treponemal test (EIA or TPPA) that stays positive for life, and a non-treponemal RPR titre that tracks activity and falls with treatment.

A fourfold fall in RPR marks successful treatment. Early syphilis gets one intramuscular dose of benzathine penicillin; late latent disease needs three weekly doses.

A pregnant woman is treated the same way, because penicillin is the only drug that also treats the fetus.

cards.front: When irregular cycles and hyperandrogenism are both already present, ovarian ultrasound is [___] to diagnose PCOS.
cards.context:
Diagnosis can rest on irregular cycles and hyperandrogenism alone. The ultrasound criterion is then unnecessary, not a mandatory third test.

Scanning everyone who already meets those two features can add a polycystic-morphology label the diagnosis does not need.

In adolescents there is still no agreed ultrasound definition, so morphology is not used at that age.

cards.front: A static or slowing fundal height across antenatal visits is an indication for a fetal growth [___].
cards.context:
Fundal height only screens. A low reading or a static or slowing trend is a positive screen, even after a normal CTG, which reflects only the fetal heart rate at the time.

The scan measures fetal size and liquor, with umbilical artery Doppler for placental function.

cards.front: APGAR components (each 0-2, total 0-10): Appearance (colour), Pulse, Grimace (reflex), Activity (tone), Respiration. Assessed at [___] minutes after birth and again at 5 minutes.
cards.context:
APGAR is a 5-component bedside assessment at 1 and 5 min (and q5min if low).

It documents the infant's condition and response to resuscitation — it does NOT trigger resuscitation, which is guided by breathing, heart rate and tone assessed within seconds of birth (AAP/ACOG).

The ranges (7-10 vigorous, 4-6 moderately depressed, 0-3 severely depressed) describe status, not a resuscitation recipe.

cards.front: Average expected weight gain in a normal-BMI singleton pregnancy is approximately [___] kg, with most gained after 20 weeks.
cards.context:
The 12.5 kg figure is an average for a normal-BMI singleton pregnancy; IOM ranges scale by pre-pregnancy BMI: underweight (BMI <18.5) 12.5-18 kg, normal (18.5-24.9) 11.5-16 kg, overweight (25-29.9) 7-11.5 kg.

Breakdown: only ~3.5 kg is fetus; rest is amniotic fluid (~1.5 kg), uterus (~1 kg), breasts (~1 kg), plasma volume + maternal fat stores (~5 kg).

cards.front: Couvelaire uterus is blood infiltration of the myometrium from severe placental abruption, causing uterine [___] and PPH; risk of DIC from disrupted decidua.
cards.context:
Couvelaire uterus (uteroplacental apoplexy) is the visual signature of severe placental abruption at caesarean — blood has dissected from retroplacental haematoma into myometrium, producing a purple, bruised uterus.

Severe abruption also releases tissue factor + procoagulants from disrupted decidua → DIC (consumptive coagulopathy: falling platelets, falling fibrinogen, raised D-dimer, prolonged INR/APTT).

Hysterectomy may be unavoidable if uterotonics, B-Lynch, UAE all fail.

cards.front: Neonatal resuscitation: chest compressions if HR remains <[___] after 30 seconds of effective positive pressure ventilation; ratio is 3:1 (compressions to breaths).
cards.context:
Chest compressions added when HR <60 despite 30 sec of effective PPV. 3:1 ratio (3 compressions to 1 ventilation, ~120 events/min) maximises ventilation in the respiratory-arrest p.

Technique: two-thumb encircling hands (thumbs over lower sternum, fingers around the back), depth ⅓ of AP chest diameter, smooth rhythm. Reassess HR q30 sec.

cards.front: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months and continued breastfeeding with complementary foods until at least [___] years.
cards.context:
The benefit is dose-dependent: longer exclusive breastfeeding means lower infant mortality, fewer episodes of gastroenteritis and otitis media, less atopy and obesity, and better cognitive outcomes.

Mothers gain reduced breast and ovarian cancer risk.

Australian uptake falls off fast — ~60% exclusive at discharge but only ~25% by 6 months, driven by return-to-work pressure, formula marketing, and unsupported lactation.

cards.front: Postnatal mood spectrum: baby blues peak at days 3-5 and self-resolve; postnatal depression peaks at [___] months. Screen with EPDS.
cards.context:
Postnatal mood disorders form a clinical spectrum and are separated by timing, severity and loss of reality testing.

Baby blues (70-80%, days 3-5, self-limiting tearfulness) — reassurance, support, monitoring.

Postnatal depression usually emerges later, often around 3-6 months, and is screened with the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS).

cards.front: Pregnancy increases venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk by approximately [___]× during pregnancy; the postpartum risk is even higher in the first 6 weeks.
cards.context:
Pregnancy is a physiologically prothrombotic state — estrogen-driven hepatic synthesis of clotting factors (II, VII, VIII, X, fibrinogen) rises, fibrinolysis falls (raised PAI-1 and PAI-2 from placenta).

The result is a 4-5× rise in VTE risk during pregnancy itself (RCOG), and an even higher 20-80× rise in the first 6 weeks postpartum.

VTE remains a leading direct cause of maternal mortality in Australia. Risk-stratify every pregnant patient at booking and again after each clinical change.
